title: Artificial Analysis 评测：Grok Voice 3.0 以 86.9 分登顶语音到语音模型榜
content:
Grok Voice 3.0 在 Artificial Analysis Speech to Speech Index 以 86.9 分首秀登顶，领先 GPT-Live-1（Astra, medium）的 83.2 和 Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking（High）的 82.6，较 Grok Voice 2.0 提升 5.6 分。
第三方评测机构给出 Grok Voice 3.0 与竞品在语音智能体、推理、延迟和成本上的具体分数，便于横向选型。
SpaceXAI 的 Grok Voice 3.0 是新的领先语音到语音模型，在 Artificial Analysis 语音到语音指数上以 86.9 首次亮相即排名第 1，同时在延迟方面也很有竞争力
Grok Voice 3.0 是 @SpaceXSI 的 Grok Voice 2.0 的继任者，这是一款可通过 SpaceXAI Realtime API 使用的语音到语音模型，价格为每分钟 $0.08。我们通过 SpaceXAI Realtime API 使用 Rex 语音对 Grok Voice 3.0 进行了评估。
关键要点：
➤ 语音到语音指数：Grok Voice 3.0 以 86.9 首次亮相即排名第 1，领先于 GPT-Live-1（Astra，medium）的 83.2、Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking（High）的 82.6 和 GPT-Live-1（Sol，low）的 80.1。它高于 Grok Voice 2.0 的 81.3（+5.6 分）和 Grok Voice 1.0 的 73.7（+13.2 分），后者发布至今还不到六个月。该指数平均了语音推理（Big Bench Audio）、智能体性能（Tau Voice）、Arena 偏好和任务成功率
➤ 语音智能体 Arena：Grok Voice 3.0 在偏好方面以 Elo 1070 排名第 3，落后于 Gemini 3.1 Flash Live Minimal（1100）和 Gemini 3.8 Live（1088），领先于 GPT-Live-1（Sol，low）的 1057，并以 94.8% 的任务成功率排名第 1，为榜单最高，略高于 Grok Voice 2.0 的 94.6%。Grok Voice 2.0 以 Elo 1011 落后
➤ Tau Voice：Grok Voice 3.0 在我们实现的 Tau Voice 基准上以 71.6% 排名第 2，落后于 GPT-Live-1（Astra，medium）的 74.5%，领先于 Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking（High）的 68.6% 和 GPT-Live-1（Sol，low）的 59.3%——高于 Grok Voice 2.0 的 56.5%
➤ Big Bench Audio：Grok Voice 3.0 在音频推理上得分 98.5%，领先于 Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking（High）的 97.7% 和 Grok Voice 2.0 的 97.2%
➤ 速度：在 Big Bench Audio 上，Grok Voice 3.0 的平均首次音频时间为 0.81 秒，明显领先于 GPT-Live-1（Sol，low）的 1.24 秒、GPT-Live-1（Astra，medium）的 1.34 秒和 Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking（High）的 1.35 秒，但慢于 Grok Voice 2.0 的 0.70 秒
➤ 成本：Grok Voice 3.0 的输入音频成本为每小时 $4.80，与 Grok Voice 2.0 相同。这高于 GPT-Live-1（Sol，low）的 $4.47 和 Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking（High）的 $3.50，低于 GPT-Live-1（Astra，medium）的 $5.83，并且比 GPT-Realtime-2.1 High 的 $10.75 便宜约 2.2 倍
祝贺 @elonmusk 和 @SpaceXSI 团队 🚀

report.summary: Grok Voice 3.0 debuts at 86.9 on Artificial Analysis' Speech-to-Speech Index, topping GPT-Live-1 (83.2) and Gemini 3.8 Live (82.6) with the highest task success rate.
report.background: Voice-to-speech models have become the new battleground for realtime AI agents, as assistants move from typed prompts to fluid, interruptible spoken conversation. Over the past year, OpenAI, Google and xAI have all shipped realtime audio APIs that stream audio in and audio out, collapsing the old three-stage pipeline of speech recognition, text reasoning and text-to-speech into a single end-to-end model. That shift cuts latency but makes quality harder to measure, which is why third-party indices such as Artificial Analysis' Speech-to-Speech Index have become reference points for buyers. The index blends audio reasoning (Big Bench Audio), agentic tool use (Tau Voice), human preference arena Elo and task success rate, giving a composite picture. Competition is fierce and fast: Grok Voice 1.0 launched less than six months before this release, and each vendor now iterates on roughly quarterly cadences.
key_points: Composite lead: Grok Voice 3.0 scores 86.9 on the Speech-to-Speech Index, ahead of GPT-Live-1 (Astra, medium) at 83.2, Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking (High) at 82.6 and GPT-Live-1 (Sol, low) at 80.1. That is +5.6 over Grok Voice 2.0 and +13.2 over Grok Voice 1.0, which launched under six months ago.

Reasoning and task reliability: it posts 98.5% on Big Bench Audio audio reasoning, the top score, and a 94.8% task success rate, also first place, edging Grok Voice 2.0's 94.6%. On the harder Tau Voice agentic benchmark it ranks second at 71.6%, behind GPT-Live-1 (Astra) at 74.5% but far ahead of its predecessor's 56.5%.

Preference and latency: in the Voice Agent Arena, human preference puts it third at Elo 1070, behind two Gemini configurations but ahead of GPT-Live-1 (Sol, low). Its average time-to-first-audio of 0.81 seconds on Big Bench Audio beats all rivals (1.24-1.35s), though it is slower than Grok Voice 2.0's 0.70s.

Pricing: input audio costs $4.80 per hour via the realtime API, unchanged from Grok Voice 2.0. That is roughly 2.2x cheaper than GPT-Realtime-2.1 High ($10.75/hour) and below GPT-Live-1 (Astra, medium) at $5.83, but above Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking at $3.50 and GPT-Live-1 (Sol, low) at $4.47.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this is a reminder that voice is no longer a feature bolted onto a chatbot but a benchmarked product category with its own leaderboard, and that leadership can change within a single quarter. For developers, the practical message is that no single model wins everywhere: Grok Voice 3.0 leads on reasoning, task completion and speed, while Gemini still wins on human preference and cost, and GPT-Live-1 leads the hardest agentic tool-use test. Teams building voice agents should route by workload rather than defaulting to one vendor, and should treat latency and per-hour audio pricing as first-class design constraints. For regular users, expect noticeably snappier, more reliable spoken assistants that can actually finish multi-step tasks without repeating themselves.
report.tools: To follow up, watch the Artificial Analysis Speech-to-Speech Index for ongoing head-to-head scores, and the underlying suites Big Bench Audio and Tau Voice if you want to run your own evaluations. For building, try the realtime voice APIs from xAI, OpenAI and Google, and open frameworks such as LiveKit Agents, Pipecat and Vocode for low-latency orchestration. LiveKit's and Pipecat's open source repos include latency instrumentation that mirrors the time-to-first-audio metric used here.
